options.text: There is a custom I have heard of…
[character] deserves no honor, in this life or the next.

events.text: [character] lies before you, surrounded by his fallen guard. Although it was a vicious struggle to the last, the leader ultimately fell to your. What will you do with the fallen [title]?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Battle Diary

options.text: I will study the documents to see what I might learn.
Have our military strategists review the works.
These do not belong to us. See them returned to [rival].

events.text: With the violence of battle subsided, the land lies scarred and still. Picking through the grim leavings of your skirmish with [character] and his forces, your troops uncover a series of diagrams and detailed notes among the debris. Closer inspection reveals the collection to be the battle diary of the defeated general.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Battlefield Duel
events.text: News of the battle reaches [city] before the week is out. Reports say that it was a clash of minds unlike anything seen before, each general wielding their knowledge of tactical maneuvers in a duel of minds. The fight was decided with a final ploy in which [character] faked the retreat of his troops, whilst keeping them organized enough to reform at a moment’s notice. As the enemy rushed forwards, the [rival] units pulled back together and decimated the enemy forces.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Battlefield Duel

options.text: Make an example of the body.

events.text: <p.is_sub.S0=SUBJECT_LEADER_US>[character]’s spear narrowly misses your right shoulder as draw your arm back. Using the momentum from your pulled back arm, you swing your weapon forwards and up into the underside of his outstretched arm. The connection with flesh brings forth a cry of pain and you pull back to a grounded position with your shield raised by instinct. [character] is slowed but not down. Another attack fumbles and you take your chance, striking his leg. He drops to the floor, finally defeated. Victory is yours. Will you kill [character], or spare his life?<else>The duel is too close to call. [character] and [character] exchange blows, neither willing to back down. Suddenly, an opening appears and [character] swings his weapon upwards into the underside of [character]’s outstretched arm. The connection with flesh brings forth a cry of pain. But [character] is not down. He charges forwards with a cry and swings wildly. [character] calmly blocks the attack and strikes at [character]’s leg with precise and professional movements. He drops to the floor, finally defeated. Victory is yours. Should [character] kill [character], or spare his life?<end>

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Battlefield Duel

options.text: Rigorous training will avoid future wounds.

events.text: [character] faces down [character], the sweat slicking down his hair and sticking the fabric under his armor to his skin. Not that he notices; every ounce of his being is focused on his opponent’s slightest movement. Suddenly, [character] lurches towards [character], weight shifting from right to left foot as he tries to find an opening. The familiar thud of metal being absorbed by leather lets [character] know that his armor held, but the weight of the blow knocks [character] off balance and in the opening a second blow finds a crack in his armor and pushes through. However, [character] miscalculated. The thrust only grazed [character] and now [character] is too close to maneuver. With a swing, [character] slams his shield into [character]’s helmet with as much force as he can muster. [character] falls backwards, helmet severely dented. The duel ends but the battle continues. [character] may have won this fight, but the wound aches his side.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Battlefield Duel

options.text: Mourn the loss of a great man.
Commemorate their duel with a statue in the capital.

events.text: [character] and [character] clash with the sharp sound of metal on metal. Their blows fall heavy and fast, while soldiers from both sides watch in awe. Even as the tiredness seeps into their muscles, each blow is precise, each one intended to kill. A small stumble provides a moment of opening for [character], and his blade punctures [character]’s side, slipping between his armor under the arm. It is done, or so [character] thinks. As he steps forwards for the killing blow, [character] swings wildly, catching [character] across the face. A hush descends as the generals lay still. The opposing armies quietly draw back, each to honor their own.
